What do other customers say in their reviews, does it actually hold up?

You’re smart to ask that, especially after being disappointed before.

Based on the reviews we see, quality generally does hold up well across our products, and people tend to be very vocal when something works for them. A few examples:

• Fertilizer: For OmniMeal Natural Fertilizer & Nourishing Plant Food, customers talk about stronger growth and more blooms than they’ve seen with other products. One reviewer said they had “never seen such green leaves and beautiful blooms” and now neighbors are asking what they’re using.

• Roses: Our roses are grown on their own roots, and many reviews highlight how quickly they establish and bloom. For example, the Carding Mill™ rose has reviews from people in challenging areas (like NYC with common disease pressure) saying it’s blooming beautifully while other roses in the same garden are struggling.

• Tools & supplies: Even simple tools like the 3-in-1 Soil Meter and LoopLock Garden Ties™ get consistent 5-star or very positive reviews about being sturdy, genuinely useful, and making rose care easier.

On top of that, every rose comes with a one-year guarantee, and other products have their own guarantees, so if something doesn’t perform as expected, you can reach out and we’ll help troubleshoot.

Is there anything I should pair it with to get the best result?

Great question, especially since you want this to really succeed.

If you’re getting a rose, the best “pairing” is a simple nutrient + soil support combo:

All-in-one starter set
The Get Growing Bundle is our go-to because it combines our favorite amendments in one package so you don’t have to guess. It’s designed to help new roses establish strong roots and handle different conditions.

Soil support
Mint compost (included in the bundle) helps:

Improve soil structure around the roots
Hold moisture more evenly
Protect roots as the plant settles in

Gentle, ongoing feeding
Our Founders fish fertilizer (also in the bundle) is a great first-year fertilizer. You can apply it about every 4 weeks during the growing season to support steady growth and blooms without being harsh.

These pair especially well with a new rose because they focus on root health and slow, steady nutrition, which is key for long-term quality.
